one_liner: Header-only lock-free SPSC queue for C++11; beats a mutex-guarded queue by ~7x in ping-pong latency.
what_it_does: Passes objects between exactly one producer thread and one consumer thread without locking. API is shaped like std::queue (enqueue/try_enqueue, try_dequeue, peek, size_approx) but is its own templated class, not a drop-in swap for a std::mutex+std::queue call site. Also ships a blocking variant (BlockingReaderWriterQueue, wait_dequeue) and a fixed-capacity circular-buffer sibling (readerwritercircularbuffer.h).
how_it_is_fast: Queue-of-queues design: a circular-linked-list of fixed-size 'block' ring buffers, with the producer owning tail indices/pointers and the consumer owning front indices/pointers so each thread only writes its own state. Enqueue/dequeue are wait-free (no CAS loop, no spinning), O(1) except when a new block must be malloc'd. On x86/x86-64 the required memory barriers compile down to no-ops, so the hot path is just plain loads and stores.
when_to_use: Exactly one fixed producer thread and one fixed consumer thread that never swap roles
Passing small, cheaply-movable/copyable values (counters, pointers, small structs) between the two threads
Need sub-100ns round-trip latency and want to avoid std::mutex-guarded queue overhead entirely
Want a 2-file header-only drop with zero build step and zero external dependencies
Running on x86/x86-64 (the best-tested and only architecture the author has directly validated)
when_not_to_use: Need multiple producers or multiple consumers (use the same author's moodycamel::ConcurrentQueue instead)
Threads need to switch producer/consumer roles at runtime, or use the queue from more than 2 threads

Targeting AArch64 or another weakly-ordered architecture on an old pinned commit: size_approx() had a real SIGSEGV race from a missing release fence before publishing new blocks (issue #171); fixed, but verify the fix is in your pinned commit
Need a version-pinned release: the project ships no tags (open issues #144/#146 ask for one), so you pin a raw commit SHA
Destroying the queue while a thread is blocked in wait_dequeue() is undefined behavior — risky in ad-hoc shutdown paths

integration.dependencies: none (readerwriterqueue.h + atomicops.h; atomicops.h embeds Preshing's zlib-licensed semaphore for the blocking variant)
integration.min_toolchain: C++11; MSVC2010+, GCC 4.7+ (GCC 4.6 has a fence bug), ICC 13+
integration.platforms: x86/x86-64 (only architecture directly tested by the author); portable to ARM/PowerPC per code comments but AArch64 had a confirmed weak-memory-model race, fixed in a recent commit (issue #171); explicitly not for DEC Alpha
integration.thread_safety: Exactly one producer thread + one consumer thread, fixed roles; concurrent/re-entrant calls from more than one thread per role trip a debug-only assert (issues #151/#162) and are undefined in release builds
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same problem domain and a std::queue-like API shape, but SPSC-only and a different type, so call sites using std::mutex + std::queue must be rewritten, not just relinked

gotchas: size_approx() could dereference a null block on AArch64 due to a missing release fence in inner_enqueue() (issue #171) — fixed, but confirm the fix predates whatever commit you pin
Plain enqueue() can malloc and grow the queue on demand; only try_enqueue() is guaranteed never to allocate
Destroying the queue while a thread is blocked in wait_dequeue()/wait_dequeue_timed() is undefined behavior
No tagged releases exist (open issues #144, #146); vendor a commit SHA rather than expecting semver tags
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick this over atomic_queue, Boost.Lockfree, xenium, or oneTBB when you want the smallest possible header-only footprint (2 files, no build) purely for the SPSC case and don't need bounded/blocking strategy choices or MPMC support; atomic_queue's AtomicQueue (42ns) and OptimistAtomicQueue (33ns) edge it out slightly in the same shootout, so pick those instead if the last few nanoseconds matter more than dependency count.
verified_claims_summary: In the independent max0x7ba/atomic_queue SPSC ping-pong shootout (gcc-14.2.0, -O3 -march=native -mtune=native, AMD Ryzen 5950X, readerwriterqueue commit 2ae710d), moodycamel::ReaderWriterQueue measured a 43ns mean round-trip latency versus 320ns for a mutex-guarded ring buffer used as the std::mutex baseline (~7.4x lower). The project's own benchmarks/bench.cpp never compares against std::mutex at all — only against the 1024cores SPSC queue and folly::ProducerConsumerQueue.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-09-07, 4.6k stars) but ships no tagged releases; BSD-2-Clause (Simplified BSD, per LICENSE.md — GitHub's license detector shows NOASSERTION) and small enough (2 headers) to vendor directly.
